question.prompt:
An equivalent of the expression

\[ \begin{aligned} &\left(\frac{x^2+1}{x}\right) \left(\frac{y^2+1}{y}\right)\\ &\quad+ \left(\frac{x^2-1}{y}\right) \left(\frac{y^2-1}{x}\right),\\ &\qquad xy\ne0, \end{aligned} \]

is:

solutions.explanation:
Both products have denominator \(xy\), so combining them first makes the cancellation in their numerators visible. Since \(xy\ne0\), the expression equals
\[
\frac{(x^2+1)(y^2+1)+(x^2-1)(y^2-1)}{xy}.
\]
Expanding the numerator gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(x^2y^2+x^2+y^2+1)\\
&\quad +(x^2y^2-x^2-y^2+1)\\
&=2x^2y^2+2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The \(x^2\) and \(y^2\) terms cancel. Therefore the original expression is
\[
\frac{2x^2y^2+2}{xy}
=2xy+\frac{2}{xy}.
\]
This is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Combine over a common denominator
